To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
riboflavin deficiency increases the formation of 2-AAF-DNA adducts, but not 2-AAF-N7-Gua adducts in rat liver and that riboflavine deficiency decreases the formation of 3-OH-AAF in rat liver.

riboflavin deficiency increases the metabolism of 4-aminobiphenyl, but not of 2- or 4-nitroquinoline N-oxide, and that pantothenic-acid deficiency increases the metabolism both of 2- and 4-aminofluorine.
riboflavin deficiency increased conjugation, and pantothenate deficiency increased conjugation of 2-aminefluorene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary ribo­ flavin and pantothenate on the metabolism of the carcinogen 2-amin­ ofluorene.
the effects of riboflavin deficiency and pantothenate deficiency on the metabolism of the carcinogen 2-amino-3-methylimidazo[4,5-f] quinoline, a component of fried beef.
the effect of dietary riboflavine on the metabolism of the carcinogen 2-aminfluorene in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
riboflavin, in the diet or administered parenterally, does not protect against the carcinogenic action of 2- aminofluorene, and that the pantothenic-acid-deficient diet is a potent carcinogen.
the administration of riboflavin or pantothenic to rats on a low protein and low riboflavin diet does not alter the metabolism of 1-aminofluoranthene or 1-aminopyrene.
the metabolism of 4-aminoazobenzene in the rat, as measured by the urinary excretion of 2-aminoazobenzenes, is increased by dietary riboflavine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
riboflavin deficiency increases the conjugation of AFB _{1} to glutathione, and pantothenate deficiency decreases the conjugation to glucuronic acid.
the metabolism of 1- and 2-naphthylamine is not affected by dietary riboflavine or pantothenic-acid.
the metabolism of 1-naphthylamine and 2-aminobenzanthrone is not altered by riboflavin or pantothenic deficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of riboflavin on the metabolism of AAF are not mediated through changes in the conjugation of AAF.
riboflavin is an essential nutrient for the detoxification of 2-AMF.
the metabolism of 1,2-dimethylhydrazine in the colon is not affected by the presence of dietary ribofalavin or pantothenic acids.
